fixes: Ashlar cheek: the left cheek is a stack of 6 near-identical cubes, each ~0.4 m, that reads as a column of boxes and sticks out proud of the face. Concept side view has a thin stepped ashlar wall (courses 0.25-0.3 m, stepping back toward the top) running behind the rock. Use 0.25 m courses, offset joints, 0.08-0.1 m mortar gaps, and step the cheek back 0.1 m per 3 courses so it merges into the rock.

Rock face: the face is flat planar slabs with a vertical chute; concept is deeply craggy, overhanging basalt with ledges that the threads touch and break on (lookbook 05). Add 2-3 ledges projecting 0.1-0.2 m so threads split and splash, increase relief amplitude to 8-15 cm facets, and add a left/right overhang so the silhouette is not a rectangle.

Pedestal basin: pedestal is a big blob whose bowl barely shows from 1.6 m eye height; concept (front view) has a rock basin about 1.0 m wide x 0.7 m tall with a clearly visible round bowl lip and teal water just below the rim. Raise the rim lip to 6-8 cm, make the bowl 0.75 m across and visible, and lower the pedestal to 0.65 m so the threads are about 1.7 m long.

Threads: 4-8 ribbons at 8-15 mm read fine, but they are evenly spread over a flat strip and start under a plain mirror-like trough slab. Concept has a lit slot with a lip that the water pours over in a curtain of 15-25 thin threads. Vary spacing (clusters of 2-3), add 2-3 threads thickness 4-6 mm, and darken the trough top so it does not read as a metal sheet.

LOD2/LOD3: silhouette is a plain rectangle (LOD3 41 tris with no projecting basin). Add the projecting pedestal as a wedge at LOD3 and keep the 0.3 m basin projection in the LOD2 silhouette; at 61 m the object is a black bar and cannot be named.
Variation: seeds mostly shift the cheek side and thread count. Make slot shape (straight/arched/stepped) clearly visible in the silhouette (lip bow 0.15 m) and flip cheek side between seeds.
library_issues: basalt_wet shows as bright silver foil on large planar faces (specular too high / no breakup), most visible on the trough top and pedestal front; known library issue.
waterfall material on the trough reads as a mirror-like white slab; opacity/emission should be lower for the static render.
stepping_stone/ashlar cheek colour is flat brown-grey, concept stones are darker with warm edge light.
summary: Reads as a trickle on a rock wall with a basin, and the overall 1.2 x 0.6 x 2.5 layout follows the sheet. But the cube-stack cheek, flat rock face and unreadable bowl keep it from the concept's craggy, lit look; LOD2/3 are rectangles.
